subject: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>, Dr. Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups

Hi Alicia / Samir,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Requirements we captured:
- Must keep PHI/PII inside AcmeHealth-controlled VPC (no token or raw data stored in Redwood-hosted networks).
- Audit/traceability: per-request logging with customer-controlled retention policy (default 90 days, option for 7 years for specific workloads).
- Strict egress controls: only allow traffic to AcmeHealth destination IPs / endpoints; any model updates/pulls must be via offline/manual sync for air-gapped workloads.

2) Questions we promised to answer:
- How the Private (VPC) deployment handles network boundaries, egress controls, and data-at-rest encryption.
- What logs/metadata we store and how retention can be configured.
- Options for on-prem / air-gapped installs vs. VPC-hosted private control plane.

3) Next steps: 
- I’m looping in Dev (solutions) and Monica (security) to provide a short dataflow diagram and a written summary of logging/retention + egress controls by EOD tomorrow.
- Alicia, can you confirm whether AcmeHealth requires hardware HSM for key management or if KMS in your cloud account is acceptable? Also confirm anticipated throughput (rps) and peak gen token volumes so we size a Dedicated pool if needed.

Attachments: we’ll share a VPC dataflow diagram and our SOC2 summary in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups

Marissa — thanks for the recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from the security team: 

- Key mgmt: We prefer to use our cloud KMS (Azure Key Vault) for encrypting customer data; HSM is not required for Phase 1.
- Retention: Default 90 days is fine for non-PHI, but for diagnostics logs tied to PHI we need a configurable retention up to 7 years. Can Redwood provide per-route retention policies?
- Logging: We need request-level metadata (timestamp, originating VPC subnet, model id/version, token counts, request id) but cannot include full prompt text in any externally-stored logs. Is it possible to enable metadata-only logging?
- Egress: All traffic must be initiated from within our VPC. Any outbound calls from Redwood agents must be explicitly whitelisted by our network team.

Please send the dataflow diagram and the SOC2 summary; also include a short matrix showing what is captured in logs vs. what we can opt out of.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Torres
Director, Data Security | AcmeHealth
alicia.torres@acmehealth.com

Attachment: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (document stub)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>, Dr. Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups

Hi Alicia / Samir — following up with the technical answers and attaching the VPC dataflow diagram. High-level summary below: 

- Deployment modes we support for Private: (1) VPC-hosted private control plane with customer-managed networking (recommended for cloud-hosted Acme using Azure), (2) On-prem package for fully air-gapped environments. Both keep model runtime and KV cache within your VPC/subnet.

- Network boundaries & egress controls: 
  * All runtime instances are deployed into AcmeHealth subnets (we provide ARM/Terraform templates). No outbound internet access by default.
  * Control-plane comms (if you choose managed control plane) are TLS-only and can be routed through a customer-managed NAT with IP allow-listing.
  * For air-gapped/on-prem installs: model and runtime artifacts are transferred via signed offline bundles; no outbound calls required.

- Logging & retention: 
  * We can offer metadata-only logging: request id, timestamps, model id/version, token counts, originating subnet, and response latency.
  * Full prompt/response storage is disabled by default for Private deployments. If you choose to enable it, we can store it in your customer-owned storage and apply your retention policy.
  * Retention windows are configurable per-route (90 days default; configurable up to 7 years).

- Key management: We support using your cloud KMS (Azure Key Vault). We also support HSM-backed keys if/when required. Keys never leave your account in the VPC deployment.

- Attachments: redwood_vpc_dataflow_v1.png (dataflow diagram) attached. I’ve also included a short checklist for private installs.

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute tech deep-dive with your infra/security team this week to walk the diagram and firewall rules. Availability: Wed/Thu afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups

Thanks for the rapid responses — adding a couple security clarifications: 

- Logging controls: Confirming we can provide metadata-only logs by default. For audit purposes, we can create an "opt-in" path where full prompts/responses are written directly to your customer-owned storage account with server-side encryption (keys in your KMS). We will never hold PHI prompts in Redwood-managed long-term logs unless explicitly configured by you.

- Tamper-evidence & audit: Logs include a request_id and a hash-based tamper-evidence header. We can provide a weekly signed digest for your audit team upon request.

- Egress & firewall rules: The ARM/Terraform templates include NSG rules that restrict egress to AcmeHealth-managed endpoints. If you want zero egress, choose the on-prem air-gapped package; otherwise the VPC-private option keeps all runtime traffic inside your subnets and only allows outbound control-plane to the whitelisted management IPs.

Can we schedule the tech deep-dive with your infra team? I’m available Thu 10-1 PST and Fri 9-12 PST.

Monica Patel
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
